title: Postmortem Template (v2) — Incident Taxonomy + Remediation SLA Tracking
author: Chloe Martin
body:
h1. Postmortem Template (v2) — Incident Taxonomy + Remediation SLA Tracking

This page defines the *required* taxonomy + ownership fields to include in every production incident postmortem, and adds a standard way to track remediation SLAs for action items (time-to-mitigate and time-to-permanent-fix targets by severity/category/tier).

*Audience:* all engineering on-call rotations, incident commanders, and postmortem authors.

*Scope:* Hosted API and Dedicated incidents. Private incidents are included where Redwood is primary operator (day-2 ops). *Security incidents* follow the Security IR process; do not write a full postmortem here unless Security explicitly requests it.

----

h2. How to use this template

1) Create a new postmortem page using the standard postmortem workflow.
2) Copy/paste the template below.
3) Ensure all fields marked *(Required)* are completed *before* review.
4) If the incident’s category/owner was set incorrectly during response, update it here and note why under *Reclassification notes*.

*Definition note:* This template does *not* change severity definitions. Keep using the existing Sev levels and paging policy.

----

h1. Postmortem — <INC-####> — <Short Title>

h2. Summary (2–5 sentences)

- What happened?
- Who/what was impacted (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)?
- Customer impact (symptoms + scope)?
- Status (resolved/mitigated/ongoing)?

h2. Taxonomy + Ownership (Required)

*These fields are required for trend reporting, ownership routing, and SLA tracking. Keep values consistent with the taxonomy + metadata standard.*

* Incident ID: *(Required)* <INC-####>
* Date: *(Required)* <YYYY-MM-DD>
* Severity: *(Required)* <Sev1 | Sev2 | Sev3 | Sev4>
* Deployment mode: *(Required)* <Hosted API | Dedicated | Private>
* Incident Category (primary): *(Required)* <select from Incident Taxonomy v1>
* Incident Category (secondary, optional): <select from Incident Taxonomy v1>
* Impacted surface(s): *(Required)* <e.g., Chat Completions, Embeddings, Streaming, Console, Control Plane>
* Primary impacted service/module: *(Required)* <e.g., smart-routing, gateway/edge, scheduler, gpu-fleet, control-plane, telemetry-pipeline>
* Region(s): *(Required)* <e.g., us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1>
* Customer tier(s) impacted: *(Required)* <Self-serve | Growth | Enterprise | Dedicated>
* Data sensitivity constraints: *(Required)* <None | Customer-sensitive | Regulated>

* Owning team (primary): *(Required)* <SRE | Platform | Infra/Fleet | Runtime | Observability | Support>
* Service owner (DRI): *(Required)* <Name>
* On-call rotation paged: *(Required)* <rotation name>
* Secondary / escalation team: *(Required)* <team>
* Escalation channel(s): *(Required)* <#slack-channel(s)>

* Incident Commander (IC): *(Required)* <Name>
* Comms lead: *(Required)* <Name>
* Support lead (if applicable): <Name>

h3. Reclassification notes (Required if you changed category/owner)

- Original category/owner during incident:
- Final category/owner for reporting:
- Reason for reclassification (ambiguity, new evidence, etc.):

----

h2. Customer impact (Required)

*Symptoms observed by customers*
- <e.g., elevated 5xx, increased latency, streaming disconnects>

*Blast radius*
- Number of customers impacted (estimate):
- Key accounts impacted (if Enterprise/Dedicated):
- Primary API routes impacted:

*Customer communications*
- Status page posted? <Yes/No> Link:
- Enterprise comms sent? <Yes/No> Link/thread:
- Support macros / guidance used (if applicable):

----

h2. Timeline (Required)

Use precise timestamps in *UTC*.

|| Time (UTC) || Event ||
| <HH:MM> | Detection (alert/customer report/other) | 
| <HH:MM> | Incident declared (include who declared) | 
| <HH:MM> | Primary category + owner set in incident tooling | 
| <HH:MM> | First mitigation attempt | 
| <HH:MM> | Mitigation effective (customer impact reduced) | 
| <HH:MM> | Full resolution | 
| <HH:MM> | Customer comms updates (status page / enterprise) | 
| <HH:MM> | Follow-ups opened (Linear/Jira links) | 

----

h2. Detection and response effectiveness (Required)

*How was it detected?*
- <alert name / customer ticket / synthetic>

*Time-to-detect (TTD):* <duration>
*Time-to-acknowledge (TTA):* <duration>
*Time-to-mitigate (TTM):* <duration>
*Time-to-resolve (TTR):* <duration>

*Response notes*
- What slowed us down (unknown ownership, unclear category, missing dashboards, tooling friction)?
- What went well (playbook worked, fast escalation, automated rollback, graceful degradation)?

----

h2. Root cause analysis (Required)

h3. What failed?
- <technical description>

h3. Why did it fail? (Contributing factors)
List at least one factor; multiple is common.

* Contributing factor(s): *(Required)* <select from standard list (e.g., capacity, config change, regression, dependency outage, networking, data pipeline, tooling)> 
* Trigger: <deploy/config/traffic spike/provider outage/manual action/unknown>

h3. Where did our defenses fail?
- Detection gaps:
- Guardrail gaps:
- Rollout / canary gaps:
- Fallback / graceful degradation gaps:

----

h2. Remediation SLAs (Required)

This section is the *bridge* between incident response and follow-up work. Use the remediation SLA mapping to set expectations for:
- *TTM target* (time-to-mitigate) by severity/category/tier
- *TTPF target* (time-to-permanent-fix) by severity/category/tier

*Required fields*
- Remediation SLA tier used: *(Required)* <Self-serve | Growth | Enterprise | Dedicated>
- SLA mapping reference: *(Required)* link to the remediation SLA table row (or the page section)

|| Metric || Target || Actual || Met? || Notes ||
| TTM (time-to-mitigate) | <e.g., 30 min> | <e.g., 42 min> | <Yes/No> | <why / what blocked> |
| TTPF (time-to-permanent-fix) | <e.g., 7 days> | <TBD until complete> | <TBD> | <what will count as permanent fix> |

*If TTPF is TBD:* create a tracked action item with an owner and due date (see below).

----

h2. Action items (Required)

Rules:
- Every action item must have a single DRI and an owning team.
- For Sev1/Sev2, include at least one action item that addresses recurrence risk (not just documentation).
- Mark which action item(s) fulfill *permanent fix* for TTPF.

|| ID || Action item || Type || Owner (DRI) || Owning team || Priority || Due date || Remediation SLA tag || Status || Link ||
| AI-1 | <what we will do> | <Prevention/Detection/Mitigation/Documentation> | <Name> | <Team> | <P0/P1/P2> | <YYYY-MM-DD> | <TTM | TTPF | Both> | <Open/In progress/Done> | <Linear/Jira/GitHub> |
| AI-2 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

h3. Permanent fix definition (Required for Sev1/Sev2)
- Permanent fix is complete when:
  - <clear criteria; include rollouts/monitoring>
- Action item(s) that represent the permanent fix: <AI-#>

----

h2. Ownership changes (Optional)

If this incident revealed an ownership mismatch (e.g., service vs category routing):
- Proposed change:
- Proposed primary owner:
- Proposed secondary/escalation:
- Required updates (incident-bot config, on-call routing, runbooks):

----

h2. Appendix

h3. Links
- Incident Slack channel:
- Dashboard(s):
- Relevant deploy(s) / config changes:
- Customer ticket(s) (if applicable):

h3. Supporting evidence
- Logs/traces/metrics snapshots:
- Queries used during response:

----

h2. Review and sign-off

*Required reviewers* (choose based on the owning team + surfaces impacted):
- SRE reviewer:
- Owning team reviewer:
- Support/CS reviewer (if customer-facing impact or Enterprise comms):

*Sign-off checklist*
- [ ] Taxonomy + Ownership fields completed and consistent with incident tooling
- [ ] Category/owner reclassification documented (if changed)
- [ ] Remediation SLA targets set and mapped to tier/category/severity
- [ ] TTM/TTPF actuals recorded (or TTPF action item created)
- [ ] Action items have DRIs, due dates, and links
- [ ] Customer communications documented
